   C. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 21-49 AMENDING THE AUTHORIZED
  POSITION SALARY SCHEDULE TO INCORPORATE THE CALIFORNIA
  MINIMUM WAGE REQUIREMENT EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2022

  On January 1, 2022, the State minimum wage will increase to $15.00 per hour.
  To maintain compliance with State law, staff recommends salary increases for
  those position classifications not meeting the new minimum wage and equity
  adjustments to those position classifications inequitably compacted by the
  new requirement.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-49
  incorporating the new minimum wage and amending the City’s authorized
  salary schedule.

  D. PURCHASE OF RADIO EQUIPMENT FOR NEW RESCUE AMBULANCE IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $44,737.22

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is purchasing radios and communications
  equipment for the new 2021 Rescue Ambulance. In fiscal year 2020-2021, as
  part of the vehicle lease financing with Holman Capital, the San Gabriel Fire
  Department was approved to purchase a new Leader Rescue Ambulance to
  replace the current frontline apparatus along with the radio and other
  specialized equipment. In October 2020, the fire department made payment
  for the purchase of an emergency ambulance from Leader Industries. The
  assembly of the ambulance is nearly complete with the next phase of the
  assembly being the radio equipment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 21-51 and
  authorize the City Manager to approve a sole source Purchase Order to
  Motorola Solutions in an amount not to exceed $44,737.22.

  E. ORDINANCE NO. 680, AMENDING TITLE V: “PUBLIC WORKS” OF THE
  SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING CHAPTER 50.016,

   WASTE PRODUCT PROCUREMENT POLICY” – SECOND READING AND
  ADOPTION

  Senate Bill 1383 (“SB 1383), the Short-lived Climate Pollutant Reduction Act
  of 2019, requires the California Department of Resources, Recycling, and
  Recovery (“CalRecycle”) to develop regulations to reduce organics in landfills
  as a source of methane. The regulations place requirements on multiple
  entities including cities, residential households, commercial businesses,
  business owners, edible food generators, food recover organizations, food
  recovery services and waste haulers to support achievement of statewide
  organic waste disposal reduction targets. SB 1383 requires cities to adopt and
  enforce an ordinance or enforceable mechanism to implement relevant
  provisions of SB 1383 Regulations.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Waive the reading in full; and
  2. Adopt Ordinance No. 680, Amending Title V: “Public Works” of the San
  Gabriel Municipal Code by adding Chapter 50.016, “Mandatory Organic
  Waste Disposal Regulations” and Ordinance No. 681, Amending Title III:
  “Administration” Chapter 34: “Finance and Revenue” of the San Gabriel
  Municipal Code by adding Section 34.80 “Recovered Organic Waste
  Product Procurement Policy.”

  F. CITY COUNCIL CONFERENCES AND MEETINGS EXPENSE ACCOUNT

  The City of San Gabriel belongs to multiple organizations that schedule
  educational conferences throughout the year. In response to COVID-19, the
  City Council’s Conferences and Meetings Expense accounts were reduced in
  Fiscal Year 2020-21. When the budget for Fiscal Year 2021-22, was adopted
  in June, the amounts were inadvertently not increased to a more realistic level
  to cover a gradual reopening and more in-person conferences. As a result,
  the City Council Conferences and Meetings Expense accounts are not
  sufficient to cover City Council conferences and meetings scheduled for the
  rest of the fiscal year.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council increase each individual
  Councilmember’s Council Expenses budget to $6,000.

  4

   Council Alternatives

  As alternatives to the recommended action, the City Council could choose to
  increase the accounts to some other amount as determined after discussion
  by the City Council, or choose to leave the amounts at $3,000 each as currently
  budgeted.

  5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. STATE ADOPTED HOUSING LEGISLATION (SENATE BILL 8, SENATE BILL
  9, AND SENATE BILL 10)

  Over the recent years, the State of California has been in an ongoing housing
  supply crisis. This has led to a number of bills being signed and adopted at
  the State level to help alleviate the housing shortage. On September 16, 2021,
  Governor Gavin Newsom signed multiple housing bills (SB 8, SB 9, and SB 10)
  into effect in an effort to address this housing shortage problem. The report
  provides a summary of the three recently signed bills as a basis for City
  Council discussion. This item was continued from the October 19, 2021 City
  Council meeting to the November 2, 2021 City Council meeting due to the
  late hour the item was introduced at the meeting.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council review and discuss the three
  legislative bills, provide direction to staff on the development of objective
  standards, and then direct staff to draft an Ordinance for review and
  recommendation by the Planning Commission before returning to the City
  Council for formal adoption.
